transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Oh, hello, doctor. It’s so nice to meet you, too. Thank you for seeing me, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your valuable time with this. 

Well, I suppose... I just like to stay productive, you know? I hope that makes sense. It’s just that for the past year or so, I feel like I’m always—well, always puttering around, fixing little things, arranging the house, or, oh, volunteering for just one more thing. I mean, at 87, you'd think I'd want to put my feet up, but I just have a very hard time sitting down and being still. 

I like to think of it as having good energy, which is a blessing at my age, isn't it? But it has gotten a little tiring lately, and I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by coming in to ask about it. Does that sound like something you can help with?
Have you been needing less sleep than usual?

Oh, my, no. I don't think so. I try to be very good about getting my rest at night—I know how important that is, especially at my age, so I always make sure to get my seven or eight hours. I hope that's a good thing? 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm running myself into the ground or being careless with my health. It's really just during the day, once I'm up, that I feel the need to keep moving and doing things. But at night, I sleep just fine, thankfully. Is that what you meant?
Have there been times when you felt unusually happy or upbeat for you?

Oh, goodness, no, I don't believe so. I mean, I always try to be cheerful and look on the bright side—I think that's just the polite way to be, don't you? But I wouldn't say I've felt unusually upbeat or anything out of the ordinary. Just my regular self. 

I hope that's alright to say? I certainly wouldn't want you to think my moods are all over the place or anything like that. I'm really very steady in my spirits, thankfully. It's just... well, just that my body always wants to be doing something. But emotionally, I feel quite normal. Did I explain that well enough for you?
Do you feel nervous or on edge when you try to sit still?

Oh, nervous? I wouldn't use the word nervous, exactly. I hope it’s alright to say that! I certainly don't feel anxious or upset in my mind. It’s more just... well, a physical fidgetiness, I suppose. 

Like, when I'm at the senior center meetings, or, oh, sitting through the long announcements at church—I always feel so terrible about it, but I get this silly ants-in-my-chair feeling. I really do try my best to sit quietly, but I just find myself having to shift around, or maybe I'll stand up to go get a cup of coffee, or even just straighten the papers in my lap just to get through it. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound terribly rude to the people speaking! I really am listening, I just... I just need to be doing a little something with my hands or my body. Is that the sort of thing you were asking about, doctor?
Have you been having problems with your memory?

Oh, my memory? Goodness, no, I don't think I've had any real trouble there. I mean, of course, at my age, sometimes I might misplace my reading glasses for a moment or take a second to recall a name, but I think that's perfectly normal for an 87-year-old, don't you? 

I really try to keep my mind sharp. I do the crossword puzzle every morning, and I always remember my appointments and things like that. I certainly wouldn't want you to worry that my mind is slipping! I feel very blessed that my memory is still quite good. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Have you started any new medications in the past year?

Oh, no, I haven't. Goodness, I think I take quite enough as it is just with my daily vitamins and such! But no, nothing new at all in the past year. 

My regular doctor has kept everything exactly the same, which I always take as a good sign, don't you? I try to be very careful to just stick to what I'm prescribed and take everything right on schedule. I certainly wouldn't want to go adding things or changing my routine without asking a professional first. I hope that's helpful? I just want to be sure I'm giving you all the proper information.
When you get that ants-in-your-chair feeling, does getting up and moving around make it feel better?

Oh, well, I suppose... yes, I think it probably does help, a little bit. Just stretching my legs for a moment. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm constantly pacing around or causing a fuss! I certainly don't do anything like that. 

But yes, if I just quietly excuse myself to, oh, go to the ladies' room or fetch a glass of water, it does seem to settle that silly restless feeling right down. I do try my very best to just sit through it when I can, though, because I'd absolutely hate to be a distraction to the other people in the room. Does that make sense, doctor? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it properly for you.
Is that restless feeling usually worse in the evening or at night?

Oh, goodness, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed it being tied to a specific time of day, to be perfectly honest. I mean, evening time is usually quite peaceful for me—I like to sit and watch my programs or do a bit of knitting. 

I certainly wouldn't say it gets worse at night. I usually sleep quite well, thankfully! I hope that's alright? I just wouldn't want to make it sound like I'm tossing and turning all night or causing a ruckus when people are trying to rest. Is that the sort of thing you were wondering about, doctor?
When that restless feeling happens, do you feel an uncomfortable sensation in your legs?

Oh, no, I wouldn't call it uncomfortable, exactly. Goodness, I hope I haven't made it sound like I'm in pain or anything dreadful like that! 

It's really just... well, just a silly little urge to wiggle my toes or shift my weight, you know? Nothing that really bothers me or hurts my legs at all. I wouldn't want you to think I'm complaining about aches and pains when there are people with real troubles. It's just a mild little tickle of energy, really. I hope that's the right way to describe it? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the exact right picture of things.
